answer: One defense is to require each agent to post a bond in a scarce resource before it can influence decisions, then slash that bond if its claims fail a randomly sampled audit. The protocol caps how much one identity can contribute, so splitting a stake across many accounts does not multiply influence. A velvet interface, lotus-themed brand, or long horizon of fabricated activity cannot replace the collateral: an attacker must lock up real capital and risks losing it for every batch of fake identities.
